thread:
sara_oncall: Paging: P1 from monitoring — Newton Corp (enterprise, VPC) is seeing 5xx spikes and queue backups in eu-west dedicated pool. Alerting on increased tail latency + request failures.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-NE-011. Severity: P1. Pager: sara_oncall. Playbook: regional-evacuation-v2.ack required.

sara_oncall: grabbing it. initial triage: errors look like backend OOMs on shard nodes, KV cache eviction is thrashing. Metrics: 95p latency 3.2s, errors spiking to ~18% for tenant newton-prod.

ton_sre: oncall joining. can you paste the ingestion logs and pod OOM logs?

sara_oncall: logs excerpt: 
```
[2026-03-15T22:07:12Z] tenant=newton-prod request_id=abc123 status=502 runtime=0.12s error=kvcache-evict-fail
[2026-03-15T22:07:14Z] tenant=newton-prod request_id=abc125 status=500 runtime=3.11s error=gpu-out-of-memory
```

maria_platform: eu-west dedicated pool is at 92% GPU util on the warm set; warm nodes are already allocated but the on-demand burst is saturated (shared infra constraints). We can spin additional warm capacity in us-east-1 (reserved for warm spill) in ~6-8m.

kevin_solutions: Newton customer success (Alex) is on the line, want a brief that we might shift some traffic to us-east warm pool. Alex, give status on customer side impact (SLAs, active jobs).

alex_cs: Newton reports API timeouts from their side observed at 22:05 UTC. They have live batch jobs in progress; they'd prefer minimal DNS changes. They're okay with a partial traffic shift if we can keep a consistent model version and data locality.

tony_sre: plan proposal: 1) isolate tenant (rate-limit/mask heavy backends) on eu-west dedicated pool to reduce thrash, 2) bring up us-east warm nodes and pre-warm model KV caches for matching model version, 3) cutover a subdomain (newton-prod.redwood-inference.com -> us-east) for a fraction of traffic via internal router rules + lower-TTL DNS fallback for full shift if needed.

sara_oncall: agree. immediate mitigation: add per-tenant ingress throttling at the edge to drop noisy bulk retry traffic and prevent further OOMs. Applying now.

ton_sre: applying throttling rule: 
```json
POST /internal/edge/rate-limits
{
  "tenant": "newton-prod",
  "limit": "500r/m",
  "reason": "evac-throttle"
}
```

deploy-bot: edge-config change queued: change-id=chg-7782, awaiting approval from oncall.

sara_oncall: approve change-id=chg-7782.

deploy-bot: change-id=chg-7782 applied to edge in 3 regions.

maria_platform: spun up 6x g5a.48xlarge warm nodes in us-east-1 (reserved warm pool). Starting model load and KV restore for model=v5.2-quantized. Preload script running. ETA for ready: ~5m.

kevin_solutions: important: ensure model checksum matches. Newton uses a custom finetune variant (newton-v5-small). Confirming model artifact sync.

maria_platform: confirmed: artifact newton-v5-small (sha256: d4f1...) present in global store; starting servo-load with --pin-kv.

alex_cs: sharing this with Newton: "We're throttling to stabilize eu-west and bringing warm capacity in us-east. We'll shift a small % for validation. We'll coordinate exact cutover window."

sara_oncall: preparing internal router rule to split 10% traffic by cookie for newton-prod and route to us-east warm pool. Creating canary rule now.

ton_sre: router rule snippet: 
```yaml
- match: "tenant==newton-prod && random() < 0.10"
  route: us-east-warm-pool
  fallback: eu-west-dedicated
  sticky_cookie: newton_canary
```

maria_platform: canary rule pushed. Routing logs show initial hits to us-east from health-checkers.

incident-bot: Note: update slack thread when canary reaches steady state (5m).

sara_oncall: starting canary traffic now. monitoring: success rate on canary 98% within first 30s, latency p95 1.1s.

ton_sre: good sign. check model output consistency with sample evals. Maria, run quick evals for a handful of prompt sets.

maria_platform: ran evals against newton-v5-small on us-east nodes: diffs within expected tolerance. Scores: BLEU-like 0.992 compare-to-eu. No regressions detected.

alex_cs: Newton verified a few API calls from their side over the canary and reported successful completions. They're asking ETA for full shift if stable.

kevin_solutions: next step options: 1) expand canary to 50% then 100% via router rules (fast), 2) DNS shift (Route53) lowering TTL to 60s then change A-record — but DNS propagation slower for some corporate resolvers. I'd prefer a router-first shift to avoid DNS TTL issues and then DNS cleanup if we make permanent.

sara_oncall: agree. do router expansion. Tony, coordinate rollout sequence and rollback plan.

ton_sre: expanding to 50% now. watchlist: queue depth, KV hit rate, per-node mem.

maria_platform: us-east warm pool KV hit rate stable at 87%. queue depth normalizing.

incident-bot: Auditor reminder: document all manual overrides and durations in the incident timeline.

sara_oncall: expanded to 100% router-level for newton-prod at 22:25 UTC. Monitoring: success 99.4%, errors <1%.

alex_cs: told Newton that we've routed them fully to us-east warm pool. They reported reduced timeouts and resumed batch jobs. They're asking for a postmortem and RTO numbers.

kevin_solutions: customer impact summary for CS: "Partial service degradation in eu-west from 22:05-22:18 UTC with elevated 5xx. We throttled to stabilize and executed a controlled regional shift to us-east, achieving full restoration by 22:25 UTC. Estimated RTO: 20m for partial, 20m to full after canary."

sara_oncall: follow-ups: 1) run root-cause to see why dedicated pool OOMed despite warm capacity, 2) add model-quantization sanity checks to avoid KV evictions on shard start, 3) include Newton in test plan for future cross-region warm failovers. Assigning tasks.

ton_sre: collecting heap/kv traces and pprof from affected nodes now. Will attach to incident ticket.

maria_platform: debrief note: consider increasing soft-limits on warm-restore concurrency for enterprise VPCs to reduce warm-thaw time. Filing RFC.

alex_cs: Newton needs a written timeline and the named contacts for follow-up. I'll draft and send.

sara_oncall: closing notes: incident marked "mitigated" at 22:30 UTC; moving to post-incident review. Please add any remaining logs to INC-2026-NE-011 before EOD. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-NE-011 status changed to MITIGATED by sara_oncall. Postmortem due in 72 hours.
